title: Derivative of a Gaussian product average
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v>0$, and let $f\colon\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. The function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I} f(z)G_v(m,z)\,dz$, where $G_v$ is the product Gaussian density of variance $v$, is Fréchet differentiable at every $c\in\mathbb R^I$, with derivative $h\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I} f(z)A_v(c,z)[h]\,dz$, where $A_v$ is the mean derivative of the product density.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, the function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}G_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ is differentiable at every $c$, with derivative $\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)A_v(c,z)\,dz$.
